RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the December 7, 2006/Agrahayana 16, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North-Eastern Region; External
Affairs; Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation; Information and
Broadcasting; Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj;
Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances
and Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport
and Highways; Space; Statistics and Programme
Implementation; Urban Development;
Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Amount provided to Nepal
†*221. SHRI BANWARI LAL
KANCHHAL: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the amount provided by
Government for the development of Nepal
during the last five years;
(b) whether it has been brought to
Government’s notice that the expenditure
from the amount provided by India is quite
low in the districts where citizens of Indian
origin reside; and
(c) whether Government have done any
review in this regard?
Shortage of housing units
†*222. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of  HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made an
estimation about the shortage of housing
units in the country;
(b) if so, the estimated shortage of
housing units by the end of March, 2006;
(c) whether Government have fixed any
target regarding the construction of housing
units upto 2008-09; and
(d) if so, the number of housing units to
be constructed under the said target and
the total amount incurred thereon?
Setting up of atomic energy plant at
Srikakulum
*223. SHRI SUDARSHAN
AKARAPU: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to set up an Atomic Energy Plant in
Srikakulum district of Andhra Pradesh;

70
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the State Government of
Andhra Pradesh have accepted the
proposal;
(d) whether it is a fact that the local
population in this area are opposing the
setting up of this Atomic Energy Plant;
and
(e) if so,the measures Government
propose to take to allay the fear of local
public?
Allocation to Rajasthan under
AUWSP
*224. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of  URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the overall urban water supply
status/scenario in India, particularly in
Rajasthan;
(b) the amount allocated by the Central
Government to Rajasthan under
Accelerated Urban Water Supply
Programme (AUWSP)  during the last three
years and whether it has been allocated
according to laid down yardstick;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
results achieved;
(d) whether there are any proposals
from the State Government that are still
pending for consideration; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and the likely
schedule of disposal?
Installation of hoardings on roads
*225. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of  URBAN DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that hoardings
are installed on important roads in Delhi;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that these
hoardings would lead to losing of
concentration of the drivers; and
(d) if so, the steps Government are
taking to remove these hoardings?
Performance of States under
MPLADS
*226. SHRI URKHAO GWRA
BRAHMA: Will the Minister of
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME
IMPLEMENTATION be pleased to state:
(a) the list of States giving good
performance and poor performance in the
implementation of MPLADS fund since
its inception;
(b) the reasons for poor performance
and measures to improve the same;
(c) the steps to make the administration
more active for speedy disposal at the
district level; and
(d) the decision if any to enhance the
total yearly allocation of Rupees two crore
fund under MPLADS?
NHs in North East
*227. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of  SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the names of the roads proposed by
different States of the North-Eastern
Region for inclusion as National Highways;
(b) the names of the roads accepted by
the DoNER, those rejected and those kept
under consideration; and
(c) the reasons where the proposals
have been rejected?

71
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Potential of Orissa coast
*228. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of  SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
Orissa coast has good potential in the port
sector, yet it remains to be tapped; and
(b) if so, the action plan of Government
to help the State to exploit this potential to
improve the economy of this backward
State?
Four-laning of Gandhidam Mundra
Section of NH-8A
*229. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL:
SHRI VIJAYKUMAR
RUPANI:
Will the Minister of  SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether four-laning of Gandhidam
Mundra Section of NH-8A (Extn.) of length
of 73 Km. in Gujarat has been approved
by Government under the National
Highways Development Project;
(b) the steps that have been taken for
consultancy services for feasibility study
to consider the possibility of award of this
section on Design-Built-Finance-Operate
(DBFO) basis; and
(c) if not, by when proposed action
would be taken?
More houses for Homeless by 2009
*230. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aiming at
sixty lakh more houses for the homeless
by 2009;
(b) if so, the progress achieved so far,
State-wise; and
(c) the future action plan prepared in
this regard?
Technical cooperation in space
technology
*231. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE:
          SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether America is providing
technical cooperation to India for furthering
space technology; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Inter-State roads proposals pending
with Government
†*232. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether some proposals of
Rajasthan Government regarding inter-State
roads are pending with the Central
Government;
(b) if so, since when the four estimates
of inter-State roads are pending with
Government for technical approval and
financial sanction;
(c) by when Government would accord
approval to these proposals and sanction
these estimates; and

72
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) if not, the reasons therefor and the
details thereof?
Indo-US Nuclear deal
*233. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government expect the
Indo-US Nuclear deal to stay on course
despite the come back of the Democrats in
the recently held US mid-term polls; and
(b) what implications the recently held
North Korean Nuclear test would have on
the Indo-US Nuclear treaty and of the
possibilities of Iran venturing a nuclear
device test in the near future?
Allotment of land and buildings in
public interest
*234. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government allot land and
buildings to institutions and persons in
public interest;
(b) how much land has been allotted in
the years, 2004-05 and 2005-06 to such
identified institutions and people by
Government in Delhi;
(c) whether it is a fact that a large number
of applications for such valuable land have
been rejected; and
(d) if so, the system Government have
in place to allot land to some applicants
and then reject others and the details
thereof?
Efforts for being a super power
†*235. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that China is
trying to increase its influence of being a
super power on African countries while
India is far behind in its efforts of being a
super power in the economic and other
fields; and
(b) if so, the reaction of Government on
the action to be taken in this direction during
the coming years?
Allotment of Raneri Lignite block,
Bikaner, Rajasthan
*236. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the  PRIME  MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have allotted
Raneri Lignite block of Bikaner district to
Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Ltd.
(RSMM) and withdrawn the allotment as
per suggestion of NLC;
(b) if so, the scheme of NLC to develop
this block and by when; and
(c) whether Government would allot
this block again to RSMM and if so, by
when?
Four-laning of NHs in Rajasthan
*237. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI O.T. LEPCHA:
Will the Minister of  SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the State
Government of Rajasthan have proposed

73
for four-laning of NH-11 (Jaipur-Reengus-
Sikar road section), NH-12 (Jaipur-Tonk-
Kota-Jhalawar road section upto M.P.
Border) and NH-14 (Beawar-Patil-Sirohi
road section); and
(b) if so, by when these National
Highways would be four-laned?
National Urban Renewal Mission
*238. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of  URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the National Urban
Renewal Mission Programme;
(b) details of the cities, State-wise,
which have been covered under the
programme;
(c) whether it is a fact that the twin
cities of Hubli-Dharwad have been left out
of the programme; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor, with
comparative data for Hubli-Dharwad and
other cities/towns which have been included
in the programme now?
Cheating of Indians by employment
agents
*239. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of OVERSEAS
INDIAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that many Indians
who go to foreign countries on the promise
of employment agents are cheated and land
up in foreign jails for violation of
immigration laws of which the Indian
workers are ignorant;
(b) whether Government would instruct
the Indian embassies abroad to protect such
innocent citizens from being punished by
foreign Governments;
(c) whether such cases have come to
the knowledge of the Indian Embassy in
Malaysia; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Unscientific programmes on TV
*240. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of
INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that electronic
media often telecast unscientific serials on
ghosts and super powers;
(b) whether Government agree that such
programmes have serious adverse effects
on both children's and adult's mind creating
baseless beliefs; and
(c) if so, the action being taken by
Government to stop such unscientific
programmes on TV screen?

(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;

370
Expansion of atomic energy in the
country
†1639. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that targets for
expansion of atomic energy have been set
by Government;
(b) if so, the details of these targets and
by when these are being decided to be
achieved;
(c) whether the dependence of the
country on the import of fuel would increase
to achieve the target; and
(d) if so, percentage of supply of fuel
to be met with imports?
Poduction of atomic power
1640. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that after the
World War II and after obtaining
independence in 1947 A.D., India is at the
mercy of the powerful countries in the
matter of atomic power/energy;
(b) if not, the details of the atomic
power/energy produced by India herself
and expected;
(c) how India has been successful to
get atomic power/energy from USA,
France, Israel, Germany, Japan during the
last 30 years to become self-dependent;
and
(d) if not, how this problem is expected
to be solved?

371
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Protest against not filling sands
†1641. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any agitation has been
staged recently in protest against not filling
sands in sufficient quantity below the
surface after mining of coal from
underground mines in Talcher city which is
under the control of M.C.L. situated in
Orissa;
(b) whether any memorandum has been
submitted to the 'National Human Rights
Commission' in this regard; and
(c) whether owing to these very
agitations, the higher authorities of M.C.L.
have given assurance of starting sand filling
by the 15th December?
Separation of cutting and loading by
SECL
†1642. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) the justification of separating, cutting
and loading in the tender inviting notice of
surface minor machine by SECL
Undertaking in the year 2003-04;
(b) whether it is a fact that award of
tender to the same company could have
been avoided had the cutting and loading in
the tender been not separated;
(c) whether it was a deliberate act of
SECL administration that if cutting and
loading were not separated then the
companies other than the said company
would also have participated in the tender;
and
(d) the additional expenditure cost to
SECL due to such bifurcation of cutting
and loading?
Revival of Dankuni Coal Complex,
CIL
1643. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether his Ministry is considering
revival of Dankuni Coal Complex, a unit of
Coal India Limited;
(b) if so, the action taken so far by
Government for the same;
(c) whether any capital investment is
being considered for the revival; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Penalties for using forest land in
Chhattisgarh
1644. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a subsidiary
of Coal India Ltd. has been asked by the
Apex Court to pay penalties for continuing
its operations in Chhattisgarh and using
forest land there;
(b) if so, the details of the penalties
levied on the subsidiary company;
(c) whether any responsibility has been
fixed; if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) whether the total penalty has been
paid?
Policy on private sector ownership of
coal mines
1645. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the policy of Government on private
sector ownership of coal mines; and

372
(b) whether there is any proposal to
review the current policy?
MoU for setting up power project at
Pipavav, Gujarat
1646. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of Gujarat and NTPC have signed an MoU
for setting up of 1000 MW Power Project
at Pipavav in joint venture;
(b) if so, the present status of the
project;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
project is held up due to non-allotment of
Coal Mining Block to NTPC by the
Ministry of Coal;
(d) if so, the reasons for the delay in
allotment of the Coal Mining Block to
NTPC; and
(e) by when the Coal Mining Block is
likely to be allotted to NTPC?
Additional value based services to the
BSNL and MTNL customers
1647. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Telecom Department
has any proposal for additional services of
value based in the landline of BSNL and
MTNL for its customers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Data being stolen from Indian call
centres
†1648. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that data from
the Indian Call Centres  are being stolen
continuously;
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
so far to check this practice;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
foreign companies could close their call
centres if such practice continues and
employees working in these call centres
would be effected directly; and
(d) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to stop this practice?
Submarine Cable Landing Stations in
West Bengal
1649. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of Submarine Cable
Landing Stations working in the country as
on date;
(b) the owners and the locations of these
Submarine Cable Landing Stations;
(c) whether the Central Government
have assured the West Bengal Government
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

373
in March, 2006 for setting up a Submarine
Cable Landing Station in West Bengal; and
(d) if so, the present status of the same?
Collection of Speed Post packages
from the houses by postmen
1650. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to depute
postmen of the respective areas to collect
speed post packages from the houses/
establishments;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the postmen are granted
certain incentives for this service;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether this practice is in vogue in
Orissa and if not, the time-frame within
which it would be done?
Revival plan of ITI
1651. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the financial results of ITI during
the last three years; and
(b) the revival plan of ITI including
financial package and time schedule for
revival?
Opposition of Press Note 5 by global
telecom companies
1652. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the global telecom
companies have opposed Press Note 5
issued by Government banning access to
their telecom network in India from a
location outside the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons advanced by the telecom
operators opposing remote access; and
(d) the reaction of Government in this
regard?
Dearness relief for retired employees
of Posts and Telegraph
1653. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the dearness relief announced by
Government from time to time for retired
employees (Pensioners) of the Posts and
Telegraph Department are paid to them in
time;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps Government would
take to ensure that the retired
employees (Pensioners) would get all
of their allowances in time as announced
by the Central Government from time
to time?

374
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Discrepancies in the pay
scales of employees of BSNL,
Madhya Pradesh
†1654. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the pay of junior employees
is more than the pay of senior employees
due to discrepancies in the pay scales of
senior and junior employees of BSNL in
Madhya Pradesh in the context of BSNL's
revised scale of clerks and operators at par
with JAO & JE unrevised pay scale
Rs. 6500/-;
(b) if so, the number of such senior
employees whose pay is comparatively
less than the pay of junior employees; the
details thereof, State-wise; and
(c) the details of steps taken to remove
these discrepancies?
Tension to IT sector employees
1655. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware
of the problems like depression,
tension, stress etc. of the employees
of IT sector;
(b) the steps taken by Government to
help employees come out of such
situations; and
(c) whether Government would bring a
legislation with mandatory provision of
providing corporate healthcare, counselling,
etc.?
Broadband scheme
1656. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Broadband
scheme offered by MTNL is drawing poor
responses as compared to similar schemes
offered by other service providers like Air
Tel; if so, the reasons therefor;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
scheme offered by MTNL is costlier to
consumer and suffers from poor technology
and gives poor performance in wet and
cloudy season and does not even ensure
customer satisfaction; and
(c) the steps Government are taking to
improve technology and cost to the
consumer?
Modern/automatic telephone
exchanges in Andhra Pradesh
1657. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of automatic and modern
telephone exchanges in Andhra Pradesh,
location-wise; and
(b) the details of such exchanges
proposed to be set up in Andhra Pradesh
during the year 2006-07?
Hyderabad district telecom authority
1658. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) what is the beyond surcharge period,

375
when the Hyderabad district telecom
authorities of BSNL are supposed to
disconnect the land-line and mobile phone
connections;
(b) the detailed numbers of  landline
and mobile phones of BSNL not
disconnected by the Hyderabad district
telecom authorities, in case where
subscribers have not paid their Bill
amounts even after 6 months, 1 year, 2
years and 3 years, after the permitted
surcharge period, and the details of
arrears due and recovered as on this day
and the amount spent for Advocates
charges; and
(c) the details of action taken against
these erring officials of Hyderabad district
telecom authority, BSNL?
Setting up of one lakh common
service centres
1659. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have recently approved a plan to set up
1 lakh common service centres to cater to
the needs such as Internet, e-mail,
telemedicine, online education,
e-governance, etc., in five lakh villages in
the next two years;
(b) if so, the number of villages identified
for CSC in the State of Andhra Pradesh;
(c) whether it is a part of National
e-governance Action Plan;
(d) the amount that is required to set up
1 lakh CSC in the country; and
(e) from where the resources are pooled
to meet this expenditure?
Extension of STP scheme to tier-II
and tier-III cities
1660. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any assessment has been
made by his Ministry to extend the STP
Scheme to tier-II and tier-III cities in the
country;
(b) the details of STPs in the State of
Andhra Pradesh;
(c) whether any assessment has also
been made, in view of vast number of SEZs
coming into the country, the relevance of
STP scheme itself;
(d) whether his Ministry is striving for
a level playing field between the STPs and
SEZs; and
(e) if so, how his Ministry is planning
to do this?
Availing of local code dialing system
to Gurgaon/Bahadurgarh
1661. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Faridabad is
linked with NOIDA, Ghaziabad by 95
dialing systm whereas such facility is not
available to the residents of Gurgaon/
Bahadurgarh;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor; and
(c) by when the said facility is likely to
be provided to the residents of Gurgaon/
Bahadurgarh?

376
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
3-G telephony services
1662. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that on the
recommendation of TRAI, Government
propose to auction frequencies allocation
to run third generation (3G) telephony
services to enhance its revenues;
